notes.text: This landscape handwritten sheet has two columns. The left starts with an openness calculation, continues item 5 on restriction and faithfulness, and ends with local stratifications. The right contains a cancelled attempt followed by a finite minimal-counterexample argument and a heading “3 conditions équiv. :”. The thin lower-left 4 is foliation in another or undetermined hand. There is no typescript. H’s editorial notes and following section heading are not manuscript text.

Targeted check of the opening equivalence: for a continuous map, openness is equivalent to f^{-1}(closure B)=closure(f^{-1}(B)) for every B. Continuity supplies closure(f^{-1}(B)) subset f^{-1}(closure B); openness supplies the reverse by testing an open neighborhood U of x against B. Conversely, the reverse inclusion for every B makes f(U) open by taking B=Y minus f(U). No continuity hypothesis is written here. Without it, openness alone does not give equality: the identity bijection from the two-point indiscrete space to the two-point discrete space is open, but for a singleton B the left side is the singleton and the right side is the entire two-point space. This refutes only an unqualified reading of the displayed claim, not the standing continuity hypothesis explicitly visible on the preceding scan004, which the main reader has checked. The source is not corrected.

The final underbrace literally reads B subset X minus V although V=varphi(U) is a subset of Y. The crossed diagonals of X are clear. The argument’s ambient complement would be Y minus V. Independently, the criterion “for all y in V and B subset Y, y in closure B implies V cap B nonempty” is equivalent to V being open: put B=Y minus V to obtain V subset interior V, and use the neighborhood definition of closure for the converse. The written X is retained as a source slip.

The live fork example is checked directly from the displayed formula: let X_a={a}, X_b={b}, and X_c={a,b}, with a<c and b<c. Inclusion among these three nonempty sets gives precisely that poset, so the stated fidelity holds; nevertheless X_c minus the union of its proper predecessor sets is empty. This verifies the local counterexample to deriving nonempty X_c-star from inclusion fidelity. It does not verify unnamed conditions 1°, 2°, 3° bis or 4° from other pages.

The phrase “un ouvert I_U de U” contains a visibly written U. The immediately preceding inserted i in I tels que shows I_U is being defined as a set of indices, so de I would be the expected ambient phrase. The text keeps U and records the mismatch here. The ps prefix in ps-fidèle is live, with a hyphen; retracing is not converted into a separate deleted word.

Independent order-theoretic check of the right-column deduction, under the down-set meaning of closed used by barred j: assume J is not closed and every closed K with K cap J nonclosed contains J. Choose j in J with down(j) not contained in J. Then K=down(j) has K cap J nonclosed, so J subset down(j), making j the greatest element of J. If j-prime differs from j, down(j-prime) cannot fail to lie in J, since the same argument would force j<=j-prime; hence J_0=J minus {j} is the union of these down(j-prime), and is closed. The missing predecessor of j lies outside J, hence outside J_0. A separate finite enumeration checked all 19 labelled partial orders on three elements and all 39 qualifying nonclosed J, with no failures. This checks the local lemma, not the earlier topological premise that produces its hypothesis.

The boundary containment is checked independently: if X_J-star is closed and is the disjoint union of A=X_{J_0}-star and S=X_j-star, then closure(S) subset A union S; subtracting S gives closure(S) minus S subset A. This is exactly the written containment for X_j-bullet. Replacing A by X_{J_0} additionally uses the source’s asserted equality for a closed index set; its definition is not supplied on this leaf.

For the closing a)/b) pair, the complement argument works conditionally if the starred sets form a disjoint covering family: X_{I minus J}-star is the complement of X_J-star, and a subset of I is open exactly when its complement is closed. Thus closedness reflection and openness reflection are equivalent under those definitions. The equivalence with the full condition c), including the unresolved NB abbreviation, is carried as the author’s assertion rather than claimed as verified from this leaf alone. In the earlier greatest-element situation, closure(J)=closure(j), so retaining the written capital-shaped barred J in P28 does not by itself create a mathematical contradiction. The main reader separately checked the preceding leaf’s definitions of conditions1,2,3 bis; see N12 below.

The final line visibly repeats “pour” after “et pour”; the p descender supports the second pour against both witnesses’ tout. This source repetition is not repaired. The terminal arrow is represented with one shaft, in contrast to the clearly doubled implication above it. The lower-left word des remains doubtful and is not completed into an unwritten continuation.

The earlier malformed packet was discarded after its out-of-scope rows were noticed; no other page image, witness file or report was opened. The empty payload means present unreadable ink, not a blank or absent token. This avoids both inventing a symbol and treating an unrecognized mathematical symbol as an illegible-word count.

Main-reader check against scan004: its final 3 bis condition says the cumulative X_i are nonempty. Conditions1 and2 together with that condition do not imply the order-reflecting faithfulness asserted here. On the two-element chain0<1 take the one-point space X and X_0=X_1=X. These closed pieces are increasing and cover X, their intersection equals the union over common predecessors for each pair, and both are nonempty; nevertheless X_1 subset X_0 while1 is not <=0. Thus the stated implication fails under the transcribed definitions. Nonempty strata (condition3) would imply faithfulness by the disjoint-strata argument, but the written3 bis is retained. This check neither changes the source nor claims the author intended an emendation.

Main-reader strengthening of the local boundary check: for closed F and arbitrary A, F union A is closed if and only if closure(A) minus A is contained in F. Indeed closure(F union A)=F union closure(A). With F=X_{J_0} and A=X_j-star this checks the local boundary equivalence, subject to the displayed closedness of F. It does not prove the full concluding three-condition equivalence or remove the source’s finiteness hypotheses.
